title: 5번: Earth's Faster Spin and the Lost Second
fullPassage: Everyone on Earth may soon lose one second of time. For the first time ever, scientists are considering subtracting a single second. This is called a "negative leap second," and it may be necessary in 2029 because Earth is rotating slightly faster than before. Surprisingly, without global warming, this time change would likely have been necessary sooner. The reason Earth is spinning faster is the unpredictable behavior of its hot liquid core. This behavior has been causing an increase in speed for approximately 50 years, but the melting of polar ice has been counteracting this effect. Melting ice raises sea levels and shifts the planet's mass away from the poles and toward the equator. This slows the Earth's rotation in the same way that figure skaters spin more slowly when extending their arms outward. Without the melting of polar ice, it is likely that we would need to lose a second in 2026 rather than 2029. "We are headed toward a negative leap second," said one expert. "It's a matter of when."
